text: Seabrook Town pulled off an amazing turnaround, beating Harbour City 4-2 after trailing 2-0 just after halftime [#905] [#975]. Harbour City struck twice early with patient build-up play, scoring at 45' and 47' minutes through Elias Okafor and Marek Barros, who combined smart passing and set-piece skill [#904] [#905] [#973] [#975]. But Seabrook Town changed tactics at 65', pressing higher and playing more direct, which led to faster attacks and more chances [#1361]. Their first goal came quickly after winning the ball back, showing sharp counter-attacking from Tariq Marlowe at 53' [#1103] [#1104]. The late show was all from Seabrook's Kian Romano, who scored twice in stoppage time after quick moves following regains, sealing the win [#1882] [#1906]. Seabrook had more possession (53%) and twice as many shots (22) as Harbour City’s 10, proving that patience only got Harbour City so far against this high-energy, wide-playing team.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in en

- Seabrook Town won the match 4-2 despite being down 2-0 early on [#905, #975, final_score].
- Harbour City scored two goals in quick succession at 45' and 47' minutes, both non-penalty [#905, #975].
- Seabrook Town scored four goals in the second half, including two late goals by Kian Romano at 90+2' and 90+3' [#1882, #1906].
- Harbour City had lower possession (46.6%) and fewer shots (10) compared to Seabrook Town's 53.4% possession and 22 shots [team_stats].
- Seabrook Town's tactical change to press higher and play more direct in the second half improved their attacking effectiveness and helped overturn the deficit [#1361].

- Seabrook Town’s first goal (53’) came immediately after a regain by Tariq Marlowe, who scored without any build-up passes, indicating a quick counter-attack exploiting a turnover [1103, 1104]. This reflects their 3-4-3 formation and style emphasizing wide, crossing play, which likely created space to press and regain possession high up the pitch.

- The tactical change by Seabrook Town at 65’ to press higher and increase directness (press increased from 0.66 to 0.84, directness from 0.42 to 0.57, line height from 0.6 to 0.72) resulted in more aggressive attempts to win the ball quickly and attack swiftly, consistent with chasing the game and their attacking formation and style [1361].

- The late goals by Kian Romano (90+2’ and 90+3’) involved quick regains and rapid buildup with few passes, showing counter-attacking transitions. The first was a 7.2-second move starting from a regain with a through ball assist, and the second involved a 13.2-second move starting from open play with multiple short passes before scoring. This fits the pattern of pressing to create turnovers and use direct play after regaining possession [1881, 1882, 1905, 1906].

- Harbour City’s goals involved a more patient, possession-based buildup. The first goal at 45’ resulted from a sustained 56.9-second move with 17 passes and involvement of many players, reflecting their 4-2-3-1 formation and patient short passing style. The second, at 47’, came quickly from a corner with a short build-up and a cross by Marek Barros, showing set-piece efficiency [904, 905, 973, 975].

- Harbour City’s higher PPDA (9.1 vs. Seabrook’s 6.8) and fewer turnovers indicate a less aggressive pressing style, consistent with their patient possession approach, which led to fewer quick regain opportunities and allowed Seabrook to exploit turnovers for fast counters [team_stats].
